units.zh: 梁書卷第二十三 列傳第十七
units.en: Book of Liang, Volume 23, Biographies 17
units.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 23, Biographies 17

units.zh: 長沙嗣王業 永陽嗣王伯游 衡陽嗣王元簡 桂陽嗣王象
units.en: Ye, Heir Prince of Changsha; Boyou, Heir Prince of Yongyang; Yuanjian, Heir Prince of Hengyang; and Xiang, Heir Prince of Guiyang
units.literal: Ye, Heir Prince of Changsha; Boyou, Heir Prince of Yongyang; Yuanjian, Heir Prince of Hengyang; Xiang, Heir Prince of Guiyang

units.zh: 長沙嗣王業字靜曠，高祖長兄懿之子也。
units.en: Ye, Heir Prince of Changsha, whose style was Jingkuang, was the son of Yi, elder brother of Emperor Wu.
units.literal: Ye, Heir Prince of Changsha, styled Jingkuang, was the son of Yi, the High Ancestor's elder brother.

units.zh: 懿字元達，少有令譽。
units.en: Yi, styled Yuanda, enjoyed an excellent reputation from his youth.
units.literal: Yi, styled Yuanda, in youth had fine repute.

units.zh: 解褐齊安南邵陵王行參軍，襲爵臨湘縣侯。
units.en: On entering office he served as a staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling of Qi, and inherited the title Marquis of Linxiang.
units.literal: Upon leaving the cloth he became a staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling, acting as Annan, of Qi, and succeeded to the marquisate of Linxiang county.

units.zh: 遷太子舍人、洗馬、建安王友。
units.en: He was promoted to Crown Prince Attendant, Groom, and Companion to the Prince of Jian'an.
units.literal: He was transferred to Crown Prince Attendant, Groom, and Companion to the Prince of Jian'an.

units.zh: 出爲晉陵太守，曾未朞月，訟理人和，稱爲善政。
units.en: Posted as governor of Jinling, within less than a month he had brought lawsuits to order and harmony among the people, and his rule was acclaimed as exemplary.
units.literal: He went out as governor of Jinling; before a full month had passed, lawsuits were settled and the people were at peace, and it was called good government.

units.zh: 入爲中書侍郎。
units.en: He was recalled to the capital as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 永明季，授持節、都督梁南北秦沙四州諸軍事、西戎校尉、梁、南秦二州刺史，加冠軍將軍。
units.en: In the closing years of the Yongming era he received the staff of authority as Commander-in-Chief over Liang, North Qin, South Qin, and Sha, was appointed Western Rong Commandant and Governor of Liang and South Qin, and given the additional rank of General Who Establishes Might.
units.literal: In the last years of Yongming he was given the staff of authority, made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the four provinces Liang, North Qin, South Qin, and Sha, Western Rong Commandant, and Governor of Liang and South Qin, with the additional title General Who Establishes Might.

units.zh: 是歲，魏人入漢中，遂圍南鄭。
units.en: That year the Northern Wei invaded Hanzhong and laid siege to Nanzheng.
units.literal: That year the Wei entered Hanzhong and then besieged Nanzheng.

units.zh: 懿隨機拒擊，傷殺甚多，乃解圍遁去。
units.en: Yi countered them as opportunities arose, inflicting heavy casualties, until the enemy lifted the siege and withdrew.
units.literal: Yi met them as occasion demanded and repelled them, wounding and killing many; then they raised the siege and fled.

units.zh: 懿又遣氐帥楊元秀攻魏歷城、皋蘭、駱谷、坑池等六戍，剋之。
units.en: Yi also dispatched the Di chieftain Yang Yuanxiu against six Wei garrisons—Licheng, Gaolan, Luogu, Kengchi, and others—and took them all.
units.literal: Yi also sent the Di chieftain Yang Yuanxiu to attack the six Wei garrisons of Licheng, Gaolan, Luogu, Kengchi, and others, and captured them.

units.zh: 魏人震懼，邊境遂寧。
units.en: The Wei were shaken with fear, and the frontier was thereafter secure.
units.literal: The Wei were shaken with fear, and the borderlands were thereafter at peace.

units.zh: 進號征虜將軍，增封三百戶，遷督益寧二州軍事、益州刺史。
units.en: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, his fief was increased by three hundred households, and he was appointed to oversee military affairs in Yi and Ning and to serve as Governor of Yi.
units.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, his fief increased by three hundred households, and he was transferred to oversee military affairs of Yi and Ning and to be Governor of Yi.

units.zh: 入爲太子右衛率、尚書吏部郎、衛尉卿。
units.en: He was recalled as Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Commandant of the Guard.
units.literal: He entered the capital as Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Commandant of the Guard.

units.zh: 永元二年，裴叔業據豫州反，授持節、征虜將軍、督豫州諸軍事、豫州刺史，領歷陽南譙二郡太守，討叔業。
units.en: In the second year of Yongyuan, Pei Shuye rebelled while holding Yuzhou. Yi received the staff of authority as General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, Commander-in-Chief of Yuzhou, and Governor of Yuzhou, and concurrently governed Liyang and Nanqiao, to suppress Shuye.
units.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan, Pei Shuye held Yuzhou in rebellion; Yi was given the staff of authority, the title General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, command of all military affairs of Yuzhou, and the governorship of Yuzhou, and was made concurrent governor of Liyang and Nanqiao, to campaign against Shuye.

units.zh: 叔業懼，降于魏。
units.en: Shuye, in fear, surrendered to the Wei.
units.literal: Shuye was afraid and surrendered to Wei.

units.zh: 旣而平西將軍崔慧景入寇京邑，奉江夏王寶玄圍臺城。
units.en: Soon afterward General Who Pacifies the West Cui Huijing invaded the capital, supporting Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia in a siege of the imperial city.
units.literal: Thereafter the General Who Pacifies the West, Cui Huijing, invaded the capital region, supporting Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia in besieging the Terrace City.

units.zh: 齊室大亂，詔徵懿。
units.en: With the Qi court in turmoil, an edict summoned Yi to the capital.
units.literal: The house of Qi was in great disorder, and an edict summoned Yi.

units.zh: 懿時方食，投箸而起，率銳卒三千人援城。
units.en: Yi was in the middle of a meal when the summons came; he threw down his chopsticks, rose at once, and led three thousand elite troops to relieve the capital.
units.literal: Yi was then at his meal; he cast down his chopsticks, rose, and led three thousand crack troops to relieve the city.

units.zh: 慧景遣其子覺來拒，懿奔擊，大破之，覺單騎走。
units.en: Huijing sent his son Jue to block him; Yi charged headlong and routed the force completely, and Jue fled alone on horseback.
units.literal: Huijing sent his son Jue to resist; Yi charged and struck, routing them utterly, and Jue fled alone on horseback.

units.zh: 乘勝而進，慧景衆潰，追斬之。
units.en: Pressing his advantage, Yi drove on until Huijing's army broke; Huijing was pursued and beheaded.
units.literal: Pressing the victory forward, Huijing's host collapsed, and he was pursued and beheaded.

units.zh: 授侍中、尚書右僕射，未拜。
units.en: He was appointed Attendant-in-Chief and Vice Director of the Right of the Secretariat, but never took up the offices.
units.literal: He was appointed Attendant-in-Chief and Vice Director of the Right of the Secretariat, but did not assume the posts.

units.zh: 仍遷尚書令、都督征討水陸諸軍事，持節、將軍如故，增邑二千五百戶。
units.en: He was then made Director of the Secretariat and Commander-in-Chief of all land and naval forces on campaign; his staff of authority and general's rank were unchanged, and his fief was increased by two thousand five hundred households.
units.literal: He was then transferred to Director of the Secretariat and Commander-in-Chief of all land and water forces for punitive campaigns; his staff of authority and general's title remained as before, and his fief was increased by two thousand five hundred households.

units.zh: 時東昏肆虐，茹法珍、王咺之等執政，宿臣舊將，並見誅夷，懿旣立元勳，獨居朝右，深爲法珍等所憚，乃說東昏曰：「懿將行隆昌故事，陛下命在晷刻。」
units.en: At that time Emperor Donghun ruled with savage cruelty; Ru Fazhen, Wang Xuanzhi, and their faction held power, and veteran ministers and old generals were slaughtered one after another. Yi, who had won the founding merit, stood alone at the summit of the court and was deeply feared by Fazhen and his allies. They told Donghun, 'Yi is about to repeat what happened in the Longchang era—Your Majesty's life is measured in moments.'
units.literal: At that time Emperor Donghun was wanton in cruelty; Ru Fazhen, Wang Xuanzhi, and others held power; veteran ministers and old generals were all put to death. Yi, having established the founding merit, stood alone at the right hand of the court and was deeply feared by Fazhen and the rest. They therefore said to Donghun, 'Yi is about to repeat the Longchang affair; Your Majesty's life hangs by a sun-dial's shadow.'

units.zh: 東昏信之，將加酷害，而懿所親知之，密具舟江渚，勸令西奔。
units.en: Donghun believed them and was about to have Yi killed. Those close to Yi learned of the plot, secretly prepared boats on the riverbank, and urged him to flee west.
units.literal: Donghun believed them and was about to inflict cruel harm, but those close to Yi learned of it, secretly prepared boats on the riverbank, and urged him to flee west.

units.zh: 懿曰：「古皆有死，豈有叛走尚書令耶？」
units.en: Yi said, 'Since antiquity all men must die—has there ever been a Director of the Secretariat who fled in disgrace?'
units.literal: Yi said, 'Since antiquity all men must die—how could there be a Director of the Secretariat who flees in rebellion?'

units.zh: 遂遇禍。
units.en: He met his death.
units.literal: He then met with disaster.

units.zh: 中興元年，追贈侍中、中書監、司徒。
units.en: In the first year of Zhongxing he was posthumously appointed Attendant-in-Chief, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and Grand Tutor.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing he was posthumously given Attendant-in-Chief, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 宣德太后臨朝，改贈太傅。
units.en: When Empress Dowager Xuande assumed the regency, his posthumous rank was raised to Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: When Empress Dowager Xuande held court, his posthumous gift was changed to Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 天監元年，追崇丞相，封長沙郡王，諡曰宣武。
units.en: In the first year of Tianjian he was posthumously honored as Chancellor, created Prince of Changsha, and given the posthumous title Xuanwu.
units.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he was posthumously honored as Chancellor and enfeoffed as Prince of Changsha commandery, with the posthumous title Xuanwu.

units.zh: 給九旒、鸞輅、輼輬車，黃屋左纛，前後部羽葆鼓吹，輓歌二部，虎賁班劍百人，葬禮一依晉安平王故事。
units.en: He was granted the full panoply of princely funeral honors—nine tassels, the imperial carriage, the funeral bier, the yellow canopy and left banner, front and rear escorts with feathered parasols and martial music, two sections of dirge singers, and a hundred Tiger Guards with ceremonial swords—and his burial followed entirely the precedent set for the Prince of Anping of Jin.
units.literal: He was granted nine tassels, the imperial carriage, the funeral bier carriage, the yellow canopy and left banner, front and rear guard with feathered parasols and martial music, two sections of dirge singers, a hundred Tiger Guards with ceremonial swords, and his funeral rites followed entirely the precedent of the Prince of Anping of Jin.

units.zh: 業幼而明敏，識度過人。
units.en: From childhood Ye was bright and perceptive, his judgment surpassing that of others.
units.literal: Ye from childhood was bright and keen, his discernment surpassing others.

units.zh: 仕齊爲著作郎、太子舍人。
units.en: Under the Qi he served as a Compiler and Crown Prince Attendant.
units.literal: Serving Qi, he was a Compiler and Crown Prince Attendant.

units.zh: 宣武之難，與二弟藻、象俱逃匿。
units.en: When Prince Xuanwu met his death, he went into hiding together with his younger brothers Zao and Xiang.
units.literal: At the disaster of Xuanwu, he fled into hiding together with his two younger brothers Zao and Xiang.

units.zh: 高祖旣至，乃赴于軍，以爲寧朔將軍。
units.en: Once Emperor Wu had arrived, he came to join the army and was appointed General Who Pacifies the North.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor had arrived, he then came to the army and was made General Who Pacifies the North.

units.zh: 中興二年，除輔國將軍、南琅邪清河二郡太守。
units.en: In the second year of Zhongxing he was appointed General Who Assists the State and governor of South Langye and Qinghe.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he was appointed General Who Assists the State and governor of the two commanderies South Langye and Qinghe.

units.zh: 天監二年，襲封長沙王，徵爲冠軍將軍，量置佐史，遷秘書監。
units.en: In the second year of Tianjian he inherited the title Prince of Changsha, was summoned as General Who Establishes Might with an appropriate staff, and was appointed Supervisor of the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he succeeded to the princedom of Changsha, was summoned as General Who Establishes Might, was allotted staff officers as appropriate, and was transferred to Supervisor of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 四年，改授侍中。
units.en: In the fourth year he was reassigned as Attendant-in-Chief.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was reassigned as Attendant-in-Chief.

units.zh: 六年，轉散騎常侍、太子右衛率，遷左驍騎將軍，尋爲中護軍，領石頭戍軍事。
units.en: In the sixth year he became Regular Attendant and Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, was promoted to General of the Left Rapid Cavalry, and soon after was made Central Guard General with command of the Shitou garrison.
units.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Regular Attendant and Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, promoted to General of the Left Rapid Cavalry, and soon made Central Guard General in charge of the military affairs of the Shitou garrison.

units.zh: 七年，出爲使持節、都督南兗兗徐青冀五州諸軍事、仁威將軍、南兗州刺史。
units.en: In the seventh year he was posted with the emissary staff as Commander-in-Chief of South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General of Benevolent Might, and Governor of South Yan.
units.literal: In the seventh year he went out with the emissary staff of authority as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the five provinces South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General of Benevolent Might, and Governor of South Yan.

units.zh: 八年，徵爲護軍。
units.en: In the eighth year he was recalled as Protector of the Army.
units.literal: In the eighth year he was summoned as Protector of the Army.

units.zh: 九年，除中書令，改授安後將軍、鎮琅邪彭城二郡、領南琅邪太守。
units.en: In the ninth year he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and reassigned as General Who Pacifies the Rear, charged with Langye and Pengcheng and concurrently governing South Langye.
units.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and reassigned as General Who Pacifies the Rear, with charge of the two commanderies Langye and Pengcheng and concurrent governorship of South Langye.

units.zh: 十年，徵爲安右將軍、散騎常侍。
units.en: In the tenth year he was recalled as General Who Pacifies the Right and Regular Attendant.
units.literal: In the tenth year he was summoned as General Who Pacifies the Right and Regular Attendant.

units.zh: 十四年，復爲護軍，領南琅邪彭城，鎮于琅邪。
units.en: In the fourteenth year he again became Protector of the Army with charge of South Langye and Pengcheng, and took up his post at Langye.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year he again became Protector of the Army, with charge of South Langye and Pengcheng, stationed at Langye.

units.zh: 復徵中書令，出爲輕車將軍、湘州刺史。
units.en: He was again summoned as Director of the Secretariat, then posted as General of the Light Carriage and Governor of Xiangzhou.
units.literal: He was again summoned as Director of the Secretariat, then went out as General of the Light Carriage and Governor of Xiangzhou.

units.zh: 業性敦篤，所在留惠。
units.en: Ye was by nature sincere and steadfast, and wherever he served he left a legacy of kindness.
units.literal: Ye by nature was sincere and steadfast; wherever he served he left kindness behind.

units.zh: 深信因果，篤誠佛法，高祖每嘉歎之。
units.en: He was a devout believer in karmic retribution and sincerely devoted to the Buddhist teachings, which Emperor Wu often praised with admiration.
units.literal: He deeply believed in cause and effect and was devoutly sincere toward the Buddhist Law; the High Ancestor often praised and sighed over this.

units.zh: 普通三年，徵爲散騎常侍、護軍將軍。
units.en: In the third year of Putong he was recalled as Regular Attendant and Protector General of the Army.
units.literal: In the third year of Putong he was summoned as Regular Attendant and Protector General of the Army.

units.zh: 四年，改爲侍中、金紫光祿大夫。
units.en: In the fourth year he was reassigned as Attendant-in-Chief and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was changed to Attendant-in-Chief and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.

units.zh: 七年，薨，時年四十八。
units.en: In the seventh year he died, at the age of forty-eight.
units.literal: In the seventh year he died; he was forty-eight.

units.zh: 諡曰元。
units.en: He was given the posthumous title Yuan.
units.literal: His posthumous title was Yuan.

units.zh: 有文集行於世。
units.en: His collected writings circulated in his lifetime.
units.literal: He had a collection of writings in circulation in the world.

units.zh: 子孝儼嗣。
units.en: His son Xiaoyan succeeded him.
units.literal: His son Xiaoyan succeeded.

units.zh: 孝儼字希莊，聰慧有文才。
units.en: Xiaoyan, styled Xizhuang, was clever and gifted in letters.
units.literal: Xiaoyan, styled Xizhuang, was clever and had literary talent.

units.zh: 射策甲科，除秘書郎、太子舍人。
units.en: He placed in the top grade of the civil examination and was appointed Secretary and Crown Prince Attendant.
units.literal: In the archery examination he placed in the top grade and was appointed Secretary and Crown Prince Attendant.

units.zh: 從幸華林園，於座獻《相風烏》、《華光殿》、《景陽山》等頌，其文甚美，高祖深賞異之。
units.en: On an imperial visit to Hualin Garden, he presented at the banquet his odes "The Wind-Measuring Bird," "Huaguang Hall," "Jingyang Mountain," and others. The writing was exquisite, and Emperor Wu admired it greatly.
units.literal: Accompanying the emperor on a visit to Hualin Garden, he presented at the banquet his odes "The Wind-Measuring Bird," "Huaguang Hall," "Jingyang Mountain," and others; the writing was very fine, and the High Ancestor deeply admired and marveled at it.

units.zh: 普通元年，薨，時年二十三。
units.en: In the first year of Putong he died, at the age of twenty-three.
units.literal: In the first year of Putong he died; he was twenty-three.

units.zh: 諡曰章。
units.en: He was given the posthumous title Zhang.
units.literal: His posthumous title was Zhang.

units.zh: 子慎嗣。
units.en: His son Shen succeeded him.
units.literal: His son Shen succeeded.

units.zh: 藻字靖藝，元王弟也。
units.en: Zao, styled Jingyi, was the younger brother of Prince Yuan.
units.literal: Zao, styled Jingyi, was the younger brother of Prince Yuan.

units.zh: 少立名行，志操清潔。
units.en: From youth he established a reputation for conduct, and his aspirations and integrity were pure.
units.literal: From youth he established a reputation for conduct, and his aspirations and integrity were pure.

units.zh: 齊永元初，釋褐著作佐郎。
units.en: At the beginning of Qi's Yongyuan era, he entered office as Assistant Compiler.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qi's Yongyuan era, he entered office as Assistant Compiler.

units.zh: 天監元年，封西昌縣侯，食邑五百戶。
units.en: In Tianjian 1, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xichang county, with a fief of five hundred households.
units.literal: In Tianjian 1, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xichang county, with a fief of five hundred households.

units.zh: 出爲持節、都督益、寧二州諸軍事、冠軍將軍、益州刺史。
units.en: He went out as Envoy Holding Credentials, commander of military affairs in Yi and Ning provinces, Champion General, and inspector of Yizhou.
units.literal: He went out as Envoy Holding Credentials, commander of military affairs in Yi and Ning provinces, Champion General, and inspector of Yizhou.

units.zh: 時天下草創，邊徼未安，州民焦僧護聚衆數萬，據郫、繁作亂。
units.en: At the time the realm had only just been founded and the border regions were not yet settled. A provincial man, Jiao Senghu, gathered tens of thousands, occupied Pi and Fan, and rebelled.
units.literal: At the time the realm had only just been founded and the border regions were not yet settled. A provincial man, Jiao Senghu, gathered tens of thousands, occupied Pi and Fan, and rebelled.

units.zh: 藻年未弱冠，集僚佐議，欲自擊之。
units.en: Zao was not yet twenty. He gathered his aides to deliberate and wanted to attack the rebels himself.
units.literal: Zao was not yet twenty. He gathered his aides to deliberate and wanted to attack the rebels himself.

units.zh: 或陳不可，藻大怒，斬于階側。
units.en: Someone stated that this was impossible; Zao became furious and had him beheaded beside the steps.
units.literal: Someone stated that this was impossible; Zao became furious and had him beheaded beside the steps.

units.zh: 乃乘平肩輿，巡行賊壘。
units.en: He then rode a level-shouldered litter and made a circuit of the rebel camps.
units.literal: He then rode a level-shouldered litter and made a circuit of the rebel camps.

units.zh: 賊弓亂射，矢下如雨，從者舉楯禦箭，又命除之，由是人心大安。
units.en: The rebels loosed arrows wildly, and shafts fell like rain. His attendants raised shields against the arrows, but he ordered the shields removed, and the people's hearts were greatly calmed.
units.literal: The rebels loosed arrows wildly, and shafts fell like rain. His attendants raised shields against the arrows, but he ordered the shields removed, and the people's hearts were greatly calmed.

units.zh: 賊乃夜遁，藻命騎追之，斬首數千級，遂平之。
units.en: The rebels then fled by night. Zao ordered cavalry to pursue them, took several thousand heads, and pacified them.
units.literal: The rebels then fled by night. Zao ordered cavalry to pursue them, took several thousand heads, and pacified them.

units.zh: 進號信威將軍，九年，徵爲太子中庶子。
units.en: His title was advanced to General Who Inspires Trusting Awe, and in the ninth year he was summoned to be Household Attendant to the Crown Prince.
units.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Inspires Trusting Awe, and in the ninth year he was summoned to be Household Attendant to the Crown Prince.

units.zh: 十年，爲左驍騎將軍、領南琅邪太守。
units.en: In the tenth year, he became Left General of Agile Cavalry and acting administrator of South Langye.
units.literal: In the tenth year, he became Left General of Agile Cavalry and acting administrator of South Langye.

units.zh: 入爲侍中。
units.en: He entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary.
units.literal: He entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 藻性謙退，不求聞達。
units.en: Zao was by nature modest and retiring, seeking neither fame nor advancement.
units.literal: Zao by nature was modest and retiring, not seeking fame or advancement.

units.zh: 善屬文辭，尤好古體，自非公讌，未嘗妄有所爲，縱有小文，成輒棄本。
units.en: He was skilled at literary composition and especially favored the ancient style. Except at formal gatherings he never wrote casually, and even when he produced a short piece he would discard the draft once it was done.
units.literal: He was skilled at composing literary works and especially loved the ancient style; except at public banquets he never rashly produced anything, and even when he had a small piece, once finished he would discard the draft.

units.zh: 十一年，出爲使持節、都督雍、梁、秦三州竟陵、隨二郡諸軍事、仁威將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。
units.en: In the eleventh year he was posted with the emissary staff as Commander-in-Chief of Yong, Liang, and Qin and of Jingling and Sui, General of Benevolent Might, Pacifier of the Barbarians Commandant, and Governor of Yong.
units.literal: In the eleventh year he went out with the emissary staff of authority as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the three provinces Yong, Liang, and Qin and the two commanderies Jingling and Sui, General of Benevolent Might, Pacifier of the Barbarians Commandant, and Governor of Yong.

units.zh: 十二年，徵爲使持節、都督南兗兗徐青冀五州諸軍事、兗州刺史，軍號如故。
units.en: In the twelfth year he was recalled with the emissary staff as Commander-in-Chief of South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji and as Governor of Yan, his military rank unchanged.
units.literal: In the twelfth year he was summoned with the emissary staff as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the five provinces South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji and as Governor of Yan; his military title remained as before.

units.zh: 頻蒞數鎮，民吏稱之。
units.en: He served repeatedly at several frontier posts, and both the people and officials praised his rule.
units.literal: He repeatedly took up several garrison posts, and the people and officials praised him.

units.zh: 推善下人，常如弗及。
units.en: He deferred to others' virtues and humbled himself before all, always as though he fell short of them.
units.literal: He advanced others' goodness and lowered himself before men, always as if he could not match them.

units.zh: 徵爲太子詹事。
units.en: He was recalled as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
units.literal: He was summoned as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

units.zh: 普通三年，遷領軍將軍，加侍中。
units.en: In the third year of Putong he was promoted to General of the Garrison Guards with the additional title Attendant-in-Chief.
units.literal: In the third year of Putong he was transferred to General of the Garrison Guards and given the additional title Attendant-in-Chief.

units.zh: 六年，爲軍師將軍，與西豊侯正德北伐渦陽，輒班師，爲有司所奏，免官削爵土。
units.en: In the sixth year he served as General of the Army and joined the Marquis of Xifeng, Zhengde, on a northern campaign against Woyang, but abruptly withdrew his forces. The authorities impeached him, and he was stripped of office and fief.
units.literal: In the sixth year he was made General of the Army and, with the Marquis of Xifeng, Zhengde, marched north against Woyang; he abruptly withdrew the army, was impeached by the responsible offices, and was stripped of office and fief.

units.zh: 七年，起爲宗正卿。
units.en: In the seventh year he was reappointed Director of the Imperial Clan.
units.literal: In the seventh year he was raised up as Director of the Imperial Clan.

units.zh: 八年，復封爵，尋除左衛將軍，領步兵校尉。
units.en: In the eighth year his title was restored; soon after he was appointed General of the Left Guard and Commandant of Foot Soldiers.
units.literal: In the eighth year his title was restored; soon he was appointed General of the Left Guard and made Commandant of Foot Soldiers.

units.zh: 大通元年，遷侍中、中護軍。
units.en: In the first year of Datong he was promoted to Attendant-in-Chief and Central Guard General.
units.literal: In the first year of Datong he was transferred to Attendant-in-Chief and Central Guard General.

units.zh: 時渦陽始降，乃以藻爲使持節、北討都督、征北大將軍，鎮于渦陽。
units.en: Woyang had just surrendered, and Zao was appointed with the emissary staff as Northern Campaign Commander-in-Chief and General Who Conquers the North, with his headquarters at Woyang.
units.literal: At that time Woyang had just surrendered, and Zao was made emissary with staff of authority, Northern Campaign Commander-in-Chief, and General Who Conquers the North, stationed at Woyang.

units.zh: 二年，爲中權將軍、金紫光祿大夫，置佐史，加侍中。
units.en: In the second year he was appointed General of Central Authority and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle with an appropriate staff, and given the additional title Attendant-in-Chief.
units.literal: In the second year he was made General of Central Authority, Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, with staff officers allotted, and given the additional title Attendant-in-Chief.

units.zh: 中大通元年，遷護軍將軍，中權如故。
units.en: In the first year of Zhongdatong he was promoted to Protector General of the Army while retaining his rank as General of Central Authority.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhongdatong he was transferred to Protector General of the Army; his title of Central Authority remained as before.

units.zh: 三年，爲中軍將軍、太子詹事，出爲丹陽尹。
units.en: In the third year he was appointed Central Army General and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, then posted as Governor of Danyang.
units.literal: In the third year he was made Central Army General and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, then went out as Governor of Danyang.

units.zh: 高祖每歎曰：「子弟並如迦葉，吾復何憂。」
units.en: Emperor Wu often sighed and said, 'If all my sons and nephews were like Kaye, what would I have to worry about?'
units.literal: The High Ancestor often sighed and said, 'If all my sons and younger kinsmen were like Kaye, what would I have to worry about?'

units.zh: 迦葉，藻小名也。
units.en: Kaye was Zao's childhood name.
units.literal: Kaye was Zao's childhood name.

units.zh: 入爲安左將軍、尚書左僕射，加侍中，藻固辭不就，詔不許。
units.en: He was recalled as General Who Pacifies the Left and Vice Director of the Left of the Secretariat with the additional title Attendant-in-Chief. Zao firmly declined, but the edict would not allow it.
units.literal: He entered the capital as General Who Pacifies the Left and Vice Director of the Left of the Secretariat, with the additional title Attendant-in-Chief; Zao firmly declined and would not accept, but the edict did not permit it.

units.zh: 大同五年，遷中衛將軍、開府儀同三司、中書令，侍中如故。
units.en: In the fifth year of Datong he was promoted to Central Guard General, Commander with honors equal to the Three Excellencies and his own staff, and Director of the Secretariat, while retaining his title as Attendant-in-Chief.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Datong he was transferred to Central Guard General, Commander with honor equal to the Three Excellencies and an office of his own, and Director of the Secretariat; his title as Attendant-in-Chief remained as before.

units.zh: 藻性恬靜，獨處一室，床有膝痕，宗室衣冠，莫不楷則。
units.en: Zao was tranquil by nature. He lived alone in a single room, and the marks of his knees were worn into his couch. Throughout the imperial clan and the gentry, all looked to him as a model.
units.literal: Zao by nature was tranquil and still; he dwelt alone in a single room, and his couch bore the marks of his knees. Among the imperial clan and the gentry, none did not take him as a model.

units.zh: 常以爵祿太過，每思摒退，門庭閑寂，賓客罕通，太宗尤敬愛之。
units.en: He often felt his rank and stipend were too great and always thought of resigning. His household was quiet and still, and guests rarely called. Taizong especially revered and loved him.
units.literal: He often felt his rank and stipend were excessive and always thought of withdrawing; his gates and courtyard were quiet and still, and guests rarely came. The Crown Prince especially revered and loved him.

units.zh: 自遭家禍，恒布衣蒲席，不食鮮禽，非在公庭，不聽音樂。
units.en: Since his family's tragedy he always wore plain cloth and sat on rush mats, ate no fresh meat or poultry, and listened to no music except on formal court occasions.
units.literal: Since the family disaster he always wore plain cloth and sat on rush mats, ate no fresh poultry, and unless in the public court did not listen to music.

units.zh: 高祖每以此稱之。
units.en: Emperor Wu often praised him for this.
units.literal: The High Ancestor often praised him for this.

units.zh: 出爲使持節、督南徐州刺史。
units.en: He was posted with the emissary staff as Governor of South Xuzhou.
units.literal: He went out with the emissary staff of authority as overseer and Governor of South Xuzhou.

units.zh: 侯景亂，藻遣長子彧率兵入援，及城開，加散騎常侍、大將軍。
units.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Zao sent his eldest son Yu to lead troops to relieve the capital. When the city fell he was given the additional titles Regular Attendant and Great General.
units.literal: In the disorder of Hou Jing, Zao sent his eldest son Yu to lead troops in relief; when the city was opened he was given the additional titles Regular Attendant and Great General.

units.zh: 景遣其儀同蕭邕代之，據京口，藻因感氣疾，不自療。
units.en: Hou Jing sent his officer Xiao Yong to replace him and seized Jingkou. Zao fell ill with a wasting disorder and refused to seek treatment.
units.literal: Jing sent his Yitong Xiao Yong to replace him and seized Jingkou; Zao therefore fell ill with ch'i disorder and did not treat himself.

units.zh: 或勸奔江北，藻曰：「吾國之台鉉，位任特隆，旣不能誅剪逆賊，正當同死朝廷，安能投身異類，欲保餘生。」
units.en: Some urged him to flee north of the Yangzi. Zao said, 'I am a pillar of the state, my rank and responsibility exceptionally great. Having failed to destroy the rebels, I ought to die with the court. How could I cast my lot among alien peoples merely to preserve what life remains?'
units.literal: Some urged him to flee north of the river; Zao said, 'I am a pillar of the state, my position and commission exceptionally lofty. Having failed to cut down the rebel bandits, I should rightly die together with the court—how could I cast myself among alien kinds to preserve what life remains?'

units.zh: 因不食累日。
units.en: He then refused food for many days.
units.literal: He therefore did not eat for many days.

units.zh: 太清三年，薨，時年六十七。
units.en: In the third year of Taiqing he died, at the age of sixty-seven.
units.literal: In the third year of Taiqing he died; he was sixty-seven.

units.zh: 永陽嗣王伯游字士仁，高祖次兄敷之子。
units.en: Boyou, Heir Prince of Yongyang, styled Shiren, was the son of Fu, Gaozu's second elder brother.
units.literal: Boyou, Heir Prince of Yongyang, styled Shiren, was the son of Fu, Gaozu's second elder brother.

units.zh: 敷字仲達，解褐齊後將軍、征虜行參軍，輔太子舍人，洗馬，遷丹陽尹丞。
units.en: Fu, styled Zhongda, began office as acting staff officer to Qi's General of the Rear and General Who Subdues Captives, then served as assistant crown prince attendant and Groom, and was transferred to assistant Intendant of Danyang.
units.literal: Fu, styled Zhongda, began office as acting staff officer to Qi's General of the Rear and General Who Subdues Captives, then served as assistant crown prince attendant and Groom, and was transferred to assistant Intendant of Danyang.

units.zh: 入爲太子中舍人，除建威將軍、隨郡內史。
units.en: He entered court as central household attendant to the crown prince and was appointed General Who Establishes Might and Interior Minister of Sui Commandery.
units.literal: He entered court as central household attendant to the crown prince and was appointed General Who Establishes Might and Interior Minister of Sui Commandery.

units.zh: 招懷遠近，黎庶安之，以爲前後之政莫之及也。
units.en: He summoned and comforted people far and near, and the common people were at peace under him; they believed that no administration before or after matched his.
units.literal: He summoned and comforted people far and near, and the common people were at peace under him; they believed that no administration before or after matched his.

units.zh: 進號寧朔將軍，徵爲廬陵王諮議參軍。
units.en: His title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North, and he was summoned to be advisory army aide to the Prince of Luling.
units.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North, and he was summoned to be advisory army aide to the Prince of Luling.

units.zh: 建武四年，薨。
units.en: In Jianwu 4, he died.
units.literal: In Jianwu 4, he died.

units.zh: 高祖即位，追贈侍中、司空，封永陽郡王，諡曰昭。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Fu was posthumously granted the offices of Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Works, enfeoffed as Prince of Yongyang Commandery, and given the posthumous title Zhao.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Fu was posthumously granted the offices of Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Works, enfeoffed as Prince of Yongyang Commandery, and given the posthumous title Zhao.

units.zh: 伯游美風神，善言玄理。
units.en: Boyou had an elegant bearing and was skilled in the discourse of metaphysics.
units.literal: Boyou had fine bearing and spirit and was skilled at speaking of the dark principle.

units.zh: 天監元年四月，詔曰：「兄子伯游，雖年識未弘，意尚粗可。
units.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Tianjian an edict read, 'My elder brother's son Boyou, though still young in years and learning, shows promise of sound judgment.
units.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Tianjian an edict said, 'My elder brother's son Boyou, though his years and knowledge are not yet broad, his intentions are still roughly acceptable.

units.zh: 浙東奧區，宜須撫蒞，可督會稽東陽新安永嘉臨海五郡諸軍事、輔國將軍、會稽太守。」
units.en: The vital region of eastern Zhe requires a steady hand; he is appointed Commander-in-Chief of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Yongjia, and Linhai, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Kuaiji.'
units.literal: The vital region of eastern Zhe must be soothed and overseen; he may be made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the five commanderies Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Yongjia, and Linhai, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Kuaiji.'

units.zh: 二年，襲封永陽郡王。
units.en: In the second year he inherited the title Prince of Yongyang.
units.literal: In the second year he succeeded to the princedom of Yongyang commandery.

units.zh: 五年，薨，時年二十三。
units.en: In the fifth year he died, at the age of twenty-three.
units.literal: In the fifth year he died; he was twenty-three.

units.zh: 諡曰恭。
units.en: He was given the posthumous title Gong.
units.literal: His posthumous title was Gong.

units.zh: 衡陽嗣王元簡字熙遠，高祖第四弟暢之子。
units.en: Yuanjian, Heir Prince of Hengyang, styled Xiyuan, was the son of Chang, Gaozu's fourth younger brother.
units.literal: Yuanjian, Heir Prince of Hengyang, styled Xiyuan, was the son of Chang, Gaozu's fourth younger brother.

units.zh: 暢仕齊至太常，封江陵縣侯，卒。
units.en: Chang served Qi and rose to Chamberlain for Ceremonials; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiangling county and died.
units.literal: Chang served Qi and rose to Chamberlain for Ceremonials; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiangling county and died.

units.zh: 天監元年，追贈侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。
units.en: In Tianjian 1, he was posthumously granted the offices of Attendant-in-Ordinary, Great General of Agile Cavalry, and Opening Office with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies.
units.literal: In Tianjian 1, he was posthumously granted the offices of Attendant-in-Ordinary, Great General of Agile Cavalry, and Opening Office with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies.

units.zh: 封衡陽郡王。
units.en: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Hengyang Commandery.
units.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Hengyang Commandery.

units.zh: 諡曰宣。
units.en: His posthumous title was Xuan.
units.literal: His posthumous title was Xuan.

units.zh: 元簡三年襲封，除中書郎，遷會稽太守。
units.en: Yuanjian inherited the title in the third year, was appointed Secretary of the Secretariat, and was then transferred to Governor of Kuaiji.
units.literal: Yuanjian in the third year succeeded to the fief, was appointed Secretary of the Secretariat, and was transferred to Governor of Kuaiji.

units.zh: 十三年，入爲給事黃門侍郎，出爲持節、都督廣交越三州諸軍事、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。
units.en: In the thirteenth year he was recalled as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, then posted with the staff of authority as Commander-in-Chief of Guang, Jiao, and Yue, General of the Interior Who Pacifies Yue, and Governor of Guangzhou.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year he entered the capital as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, then went out with the staff of authority as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the three provinces Guang, Jiao, and Yue, General of the Interior Who Pacifies Yue, and Governor of Guangzhou.

units.zh: 還爲太子中庶子，遷使持節、都督郢司霍三州諸軍事、信武將軍、郢州刺史。
units.en: He returned as Attendant of the Crown Prince, then was posted with the emissary staff as Commander-in-Chief of E, Si, and Huo, General of Trustworthy Might, and Governor of Ezhou.
units.literal: He returned and became Attendant of the Crown Prince, then was transferred with the emissary staff of authority as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the three provinces E, Si, and Huo, General of Trustworthy Might, and Governor of Ezhou.

units.zh: 十八年正月，卒於州。
units.en: In the first month of the eighteenth year he died in office.
units.literal: In the first month of the eighteenth year he died in the province.

units.zh: 諡曰孝。
units.en: He was given the posthumous title Xiao.
units.literal: His posthumous title was Xiao.

units.zh: 子俊嗣。
units.en: His son Jun succeeded him.
units.literal: His son Jun succeeded.

units.zh: 桂陽嗣王象字世翼，長沙宣武王第九子也。
units.en: Xiang, Heir Prince of Guiyang, styled Shiyi, was the ninth son of Prince Xuanwu of Changsha.
units.literal: Xiang, Heir Prince of Guiyang, styled Shiyi, was the ninth son of Prince Xuanwu of Changsha.

units.zh: 初，叔父融仕齊至太子洗馬。
units.en: Earlier, his uncle Rong served Qi and rose to Groom of the Crown Prince's Household.
units.literal: Earlier, his uncle Rong served Qi and rose to Groom of the Crown Prince's Household.

units.zh: 永元中，宣武之難，融遇害。
units.en: During Yongyuan, in the disaster that befell Prince Xuanwu, Rong was killed.
units.literal: During Yongyuan, in the disaster that befell Prince Xuanwu, Rong was killed.

units.zh: 高祖平京邑，贈給事黃門侍郎。
units.en: After Gaozu pacified the capital, Rong was posthumously granted the office of Yellow Gate Gentleman for Service.
units.literal: After Gaozu pacified the capital, Rong was posthumously granted the office of Yellow Gate Gentleman for Service.

units.zh: 天監元年，加散騎常侍、撫軍大將軍，封桂陽郡王。
units.en: In Tianjian 1, he was additionally made Regular Attendant and Great General Who Pacifies the Army, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Guiyang Commandery.
units.literal: In Tianjian 1, he was additionally made Regular Attendant and Great General Who Pacifies the Army, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Guiyang Commandery.

units.zh: 諡曰簡。
units.en: His posthumous title was Jian.
units.literal: His posthumous title was Jian.

units.zh: 無子，乃詔象爲嗣，襲封爵。
units.en: He had no son, so an edict made Xiang his heir, and Xiang inherited the noble title.
units.literal: He had no son, so an edict made Xiang his heir, and Xiang inherited the noble title.

units.zh: 象容止閒雅，善於交遊，事所生母以孝聞。
units.en: Xiang had an easy, refined bearing and was skilled in society. In caring for his birth mother he was renowned for filial devotion.
units.literal: Xiang's bearing and deportment were easy and refined; he was skilled at social intercourse, and in serving the mother who bore him he was famed for filial piety.

units.zh: 起家寧遠將軍、丹陽尹。
units.en: On entering office he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and Governor of Danyang.
units.literal: Upon first taking office he was made General Who Pacifies the Distance and Governor of Danyang.

units.zh: 到官未幾，簡王妃薨，去職。
units.en: He had not long taken up his post when the Princess of Jian died, and he resigned to observe mourning.
units.literal: He had not long been in the post when the Princess of Jian died, and he left office.

units.zh: 服闋，復授明威將軍、丹陽尹。
units.en: When his mourning period ended he was reappointed General of Bright Might and Governor of Danyang.
units.literal: When mourning was completed he was again given the title General of Bright Might and Governor of Danyang.

units.zh: 象生長深宮，始親庶政，舉無失德，朝廷稱之。
units.en: Xiang had grown up within the palace walls. When he first took up the duties of government, nothing he did fell short of propriety, and the court praised him.
units.literal: Xiang had grown up in the deep palace; when he first took part in ordinary government affairs, in all he did there was no lapse in virtue, and the court praised him.

units.zh: 出爲持節、督司霍郢三州諸軍事、征遠將軍、郢州刺史。
units.en: He was posted with the staff of authority as overseer of Si, Huo, and E, General Who Campaigns Afar, and Governor of Ezhou.
units.literal: He went out with the staff of authority as overseer of all military affairs of the three provinces Si, Huo, and E, General Who Campaigns Afar, and Governor of Ezhou.

units.zh: 尋遷湘衡二州諸軍事、輕車將軍、湘州刺史。
units.en: Soon after he was transferred to oversee military affairs in Xiang and Heng, as General of the Light Carriage and Governor of Xiangzhou.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to oversee military affairs of the two provinces Xiang and Heng, General of the Light Carriage, and Governor of Xiangzhou.

units.zh: 湘州舊多虎暴，及象在任，爲之靜息，故老咸稱德政所感。
units.en: Xiangzhou had long been troubled by man-eating tigers. Under Xiang's rule they ceased their depredations, and the elders all attributed it to the power of his virtuous rule.
units.literal: Xiangzhou in former times had many violent tigers; when Xiang was in office they were stilled and quieted, and the elders all said it was moved by his virtuous government.

units.zh: 除中書侍郎，俄以本官行石頭戍軍事，轉給事黃門侍郎、兼領軍，又以本官兼宗正卿。
units.en: He was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, and soon afterward acted in his existing capacity over the military affairs of the Shitou garrison. He was then transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrent General of the Garrison Guards, and concurrently served as Director of the Imperial Clan.
units.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat; soon, in his present office, he acted in the military affairs of the Shitou garrison; he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrent General of the Garrison Guards, and again in his present office was made concurrent Director of the Imperial Clan.

units.zh: 尋遷侍中、太子詹事，未拜，改授持節、督江州諸軍事、信武將軍、江州刺史。
units.en: Soon after he was promoted to Attendant-in-Chief and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, but before he could take up those offices he was reassigned with the staff of authority as overseer of Jiangzhou, General of Trustworthy Might, and Governor of Jiangzhou.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to Attendant-in-Chief and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; he did not assume the posts and was reassigned with the staff of authority as overseer of all military affairs of Jiangzhou, General of Trustworthy Might, and Governor of Jiangzhou.

units.zh: 以疾免。
units.en: He resigned on account of illness.
units.literal: Because of illness he was dismissed from office.

units.zh: 尋除太常卿，加侍中，遷秘書監、領步兵校尉。
units.en: Soon after he was appointed Director of the Imperial Sacrifices with the additional title Palace Attendant, and was then made Director of the Imperial Library and concurrently Commandant of Foot Soldiers.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed Director of the Imperial Sacrifices, given the additional title Palace Attendant, and transferred to Director of the Imperial Library and concurrently Commandant of Foot Soldiers.

units.zh: 大同二年，薨，諡曰敦。
units.en: In the second year of Datong he died and was given the posthumous title Dun.
units.literal: In the second year of Datong he died; his posthumous title was Dun.

units.zh: 子慥嗣。
units.en: His son Cao succeeded him.
units.literal: His son Cao succeeded.

units.zh: 史臣曰：長沙諸嗣王，並承襲土宇，光有籓服。
units.en: The historiographer writes: The successive Heir Princes of Changsha all inherited their domains and brought honor to their princely houses.
units.literal: The historiographer says: The various Heir Princes of Changsha all inherited their domains and shone with the glory of their fiefdoms.

units.zh: 桂陽王象以孝聞，在於牧湘，猛虎息暴，蓋德惠所致也。
units.en: Prince Xiang of Guiyang was renowned for filial devotion. When he governed Xiangzhou, the man-eating tigers ceased their ravages—surely the effect of his benevolent rule.
units.literal: Prince Xiang of Guiyang was famed for filial piety; when he governed Xiang, fierce tigers ceased their violence—surely this was brought about by his virtue and kindness.

units.zh: 昔之善政，何以加焉。
units.en: What good government of antiquity could surpass this?
units.literal: How could the good government of old surpass this?

units.en: Note 1.
units.literal: Note 1.

units.zh: 庚辰，立皇子寶義爲晉安王，寶玄爲江夏王，寶源爲廬陵王，寶夤爲建安王，寶融爲隨郡王，寶攸爲南平王。
units.en: Day gengchen: Bao Yi was made prince of Jin'an; Bao Xuan, prince of Jiangxia; Bao Yuan, prince of Luling; Bao Yin, prince of Jian'an; Bao Rong, prince of Suizhou; Bao You, prince of Nanping.
units.literal: Day gengchen: the princes Bao Yi, Bao Xuan, Bao Yuan, Bao Yin, Bao Rong, and Bao You were enfeoffed as Princes of Jin'an, Jiangxia, Luling, Jian'an, Suizhou, and Nanping.

units.zh: 壬辰，以新除征虜將軍江夏王寶玄爲郢州刺史。
units.en: Day renchen: Bao Xuan, newly made general who conquers the barbarians and prince of Jiangxia, was made inspector of Yingzhou.
units.literal: Day renchen: the newly appointed General Who Conquers the Barbarians Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia was made Inspector of Yingzhou.

units.zh: 遙光敗，入東昏宮。
units.en: When Yaoguang fell, she was taken into the Depraved Emperor's palace.
units.literal: When Yaoguang was defeated, she entered the Depraved Emperor's palace.

units.zh: 嘗與臨賀王正德及胡貴通、趙伯超等馳射于高祖前，續冠于諸人，高祖大悅。
units.en: Once he competed in mounted archery before Emperor Wu with Prince Zhengde of Linhe, Hu Guitong, Zhao Bochao, and others. Xu outshot them all, and the emperor was delighted.
units.literal: Once he rode and shot before Gaozu together with Prince of Linhe Zhengde and Hu Guitong, Zhao Bochao, and others. Xu took first place among them all, and Gaozu was greatly pleased.

units.zh: 與懷朔省事雲中司馬子如及秀容人劉貴、中山人賈顯智為奔走之友，懷朔戶曹史孫騰、外兵史侯景亦相友結。
units.en: He made running companions of Sima Ziru, affairs clerk at Huaishuo's Yunzhong desk, Liu Gui of Xiurong, and Jia Xianzhi of Zhongshan; Sun Teng, the garrison household clerk, and Hou Jing, clerk for external military affairs, joined their circle as well.
units.literal: With Sima Ziru, affairs clerk of Yunzhong at Huaishuo, Liu Gui of Xiurong, and Jia Xianzhi of Zhongshan he formed a band of comrades ready to run errands; Sun Teng, household clerk at Huaishuo, and Hou Jing, clerk in external military affairs, also joined in friendship.

units.zh: 璽書詰縝曰：「亮少乏才能，無聞時輩，昔經冒入羣英，相與豈薄，晚節諂事江祏，爲吏部，末協附梅蟲兒、茹法珍，遂執昏政。
units.en: An imperial letter reprimanded Zhen: "Liang in youth lacked talent and was unknown among his peers; formerly he rashly entered the ranks of worthies—we were not thin with one another; in his later years he flattered Jiang Shi; as director of personnel he finally joined Mei Chong'er and Ru Fazhen and held benighted government.
units.literal: An imperial letter reprimanded Zhen: "Liang in youth lacked talent and was unknown among contemporaries; formerly he rashly entered the ranks of worthies—we with one another were not thin; in his later years he flattered Jiang Shi; as Director of Personnel he finally joined with Mei Chong'er and Ru Fazhen and so held benighted government.

units.zh: 俄而太尉陳顯達、護軍將軍崔慧景頻逼京師，民心遑駭，未有所定，西土人謀之於叡。
units.en: Soon Chen Xianda and Cui Huijing harried the capital repeatedly; fear ran wild and the west turned to Rui for a plan.
units.literal: Before long Grand Marshal Chen Xianda and Protector of the Army Cui Huijing pressed the capital again and again; the people's hearts were frantic and nothing was settled, and the men of the western lands looked to Rui for counsel.

units.zh: 崔頗更事，懦而不武。
units.en: Cui has weathered many storms, yet he is soft and no soldier.
units.literal: Cui has seen much, but he is timid and no warrior.

units.zh: 其取赤族也，宜哉！
units.en: They deserve the extinction of their houses—of course they do!
units.literal: That their clans should be wiped to the last man is only fitting!

units.zh: 入爲太子洗馬，大司馬東曹掾，建安王友，大司馬從事中郎。
units.en: He entered as crown prince purifier, eastern bureau staff officer to the grand marshal, friend to the prince of Jian'an, and chief staff officer to the grand marshal.
units.literal: He entered office as Crown Prince Purifier, Eastern Bureau Staff Officer to the Grand Marshal, Friend to the Prince of Jian'an, and Chief Staff Officer to the Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 建武末，魏軍圍司州，明帝使徐州刺史裴叔業攻拔渦陽，以爲聲援，起珍國爲輔國將軍，率兵助焉。
units.en: Late in Jianwu, Wei besieged Si province; Emperor Ming sent Xuzhou inspector Pei Shuye to take Guoyang as a diversion and raised Zhenguo to supporting-the-state general to reinforce him.
units.literal: Late in Jianwu, Wei forces besieged Si Province; Emperor Ming sent Xuzhou Inspector Pei Shuye to attack and capture Guoyang as a diversion, and raised Zhenguo to supporting-the-state general to lead troops in support.

units.zh: 魏將楊大眼大衆奄至，叔業懼，棄軍走，珍國率其衆殿，故不至大敗。
units.en: Wei general Yang Dayan's host suddenly arrived; Shuye in fear abandoned the army and fled; Zhenguo led the rearguard, so the defeat was not total.
units.literal: Wei general Yang Dayan's great host suddenly arrived; Shuye in fear abandoned the army and fled; Zhenguo led his men as rearguard, so they did not suffer great defeat.

units.zh: 中書舍人王咺之與相脣齒，專掌文翰。
units.en: Palace secretary Wang Youzhi was their twin at court and held the brush alone.
units.literal: Palace Secretary Wang Youzhi worked mouth to mouth with them and alone handled documents.

units.zh: 高宗詔曰：「仇池公楊元秀，氐王苗胤，乃心忠勇，醜虜凶逼，血誠彌厲，宣播朝威，招誘戎種，萬里齊契，響然歸從。
units.en: Emperor Gaozong's edict read: "Duke of Chouchi Yang Yuanxiu, of the Di royal line, was loyal and brave at heart; when the enemy pressed him hard his devotion only grew; he spread the court's authority and rallied the frontier tribes, and peoples far and near answered his call.
units.literal: Emperor Gaozong's edict said: "Duke of Chouchi Yang Yuanxiu, seed and scion of the Di kings, his heart loyal and brave—when the ugly barbarians pressed with violence, his blood sincerity grew fiercer; he spread the court's majesty and enticed the frontier peoples; ten thousand li joined in covenant and answered in echoing submission.

units.zh: 梁州刺史蕭懿遣前氐王楊後起弟子元秀收合義兵，氐衆響應，斷虜運道。
units.en: Inspector Xiao Yi sent Yuanxiu, nephew of the former Di king Yang Houqi, to gather loyal forces; Di tribes answered, cutting the enemy supply lines.
units.literal: The Inspector of Liangzhou Xiao Yi sent the former Di king Yang Houqi's younger brother's son Yuanxiu to gather righteous troops; Di hosts responded, cutting the barbarians' supply route.

units.zh: 元秀病死，符幼孫領其衆。
units.en: Yuanxiu died of illness, and Fu Yousun took command of his forces.
units.literal: Yuanxiu died of illness; Fu Yousun led his host.

units.zh: 贈仇池公。
units.en: Grant him the posthumous title Duke of Chouchi.
units.literal: Grant the title Duke of Chouchi.

units.zh: 建武二年，氐、虜寇漢中。
units.en: In the second year of Jianwu, Di and Wei forces raided Hanzhong.
units.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, Di and barbarians raided Hanzhong.

units.zh: 誠效顯著，寔有可嘉。
units.en: His loyal service was clear and truly praiseworthy.
units.literal: His loyal achievement was manifest—truly there is what to praise.

units.zh: 不幸殞喪，悽愴于懷。
units.en: His untimely death fills us with grief.
units.literal: Unfortunately he fell and died; grief wounds the heart.

units.zh: 夫死事加恩，陽秋明義。
units.en: Those who die in service deserve added honor—the Spring and Autumn Annals make that righteousness plain.
units.literal: For dying in service, grace is added; the Spring and Autumn Annals make righteousness clear.

units.zh: 宜追覃榮典，以弘勸獎。
units.en: Let posthumous honors be granted to encourage such loyalty.
units.literal: It is fitting to extend posthumous glory and thereby magnify encouragement and reward.

units.zh: 持歸國。」
units.en: Grant him Bearer of the Staff and the privilege of returning to the state."
units.literal: Bearer of the Staff, return to the state."

units.zh: 壬辰，驍騎將軍夏侯亶自京師至江陵，稱宣德太后令：「西中郎將南康王宜纂承皇祚，光臨億兆。
units.en: On renchen, Swift-as-Steeds General Xiahou Dan arrived from the capital at Jiangling and announced an order of Empress Dowager Xuande: "The Western Palace Attendant, the Prince of Nankang, should succeed to the throne and rule the myriad people.
units.literal: On renchen, the Swift-as-Steeds General Xiahou Dan arrived from the capital at Jiangling and announced an order of the Empress Dowager Xuande: "The Western Palace Attendant, the Prince of Nankang, should succeed to the imperial dignity and preside over the myriad people.

units.zh: 二年春正月戊戌，宣德太后臨朝，入居內殿。
units.en: In spring, on wuxu of the first month of year 2, Empress Dowager Xuande presided at court and took up residence in the inner palace.
units.literal: In spring, on the first month, day wuxu of the second year, the Empress Dowager Xuande presided at court and took up residence in the inner palace.

units.zh: 己巳，皇太后令以梁王爲大司馬、錄尚書事、驃騎大將軍、揚州刺史，封建安郡公，依晉武陵王遵承制故事，百僚致敬。
units.en: On jisi, the empress dowager ordered that the Prince of Liang be made grand marshal, supervisor of the Masters of Writing, general of agile cavalry, and governor of Yang Province, enfeoffed as Duke of Jian'an, with authority following the precedent of Prince Wuling of Jin when he held the imperial mandate; all officials were to pay him homage.
units.literal: On jisi, the Empress Dowager issued an order making the Prince of Liang Grand Marshal, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, General of Agile Cavalry, and Governor of Yang Province, enfeoffing him as Duke of Jian'an, with authority following the precedent of Prince Wuling of Jin when he held the imperial mandate, and all officials to pay him homage.

units.zh: 三月乙未，皇太后令給梁國錢五百萬，布五千匹，絹千匹。
units.en: On yiwei of the third month, the empress dowager ordered that the Liang kingdom be supplied with five million cash, five thousand bolts of cloth, and one thousand bolts of silk.
units.literal: On yiwei of the third month, the empress dowager ordered that the Liang kingdom be supplied with five million cash, five thousand bolts of cloth, and one thousand bolts of silk.

units.zh: 夏四月辛酉，禪詔至，皇太后遜外宮。
units.en: In summer, on xinyou of the fourth month, the abdication edict arrived, and the empress dowager withdrew to an outer palace.
units.literal: In summer, on xinyou of the fourth month, the abdication edict arrived, and the empress dowager withdrew to an outer palace.

units.zh: 方俟清宮，未卽大號，可且封宣城、南琅邪、南東海、東陽、臨海、新安、尋陽、南郡、竟陵、宜都十郡爲宣城王，相國、荊州牧，加黃皞，置僚屬，選百官，西中郎府南康國並如故。
units.en: The palace must first be cleansed before he assumes the imperial title; for now he is enfeoffed as Prince of Xuancheng over ten commanderies—Xuancheng, Nanlangye, Nandonghai, Dongyang, Linhai, Xin'an, Xunyang, Nanjun, Jingling, and Yidu—made chancellor and governor of Jing Province, granted yellow imperial regalia, with a full staff and officials chosen; the Southern Palace and the state of Nankang remain as before.
units.literal: We await the cleansing of the palace before assuming the great title; for the present he may be enfeoffed as Prince of Xuancheng over ten commanderies—Xuancheng, Nanlangye, Nandonghai, Dongyang, Linhai, Xin'an, Xunyang, Nanjun, Jingling, and Yidu—made Chancellor and Governor of Jing Province, granted yellow imperial regalia, with a full staff appointed and all officials chosen; the Southern Palace and the state of Nankang are to remain as before.

units.zh: 須軍次近路，主者詳依舊典，法駕奉迎。」
units.en: When the army draws near on the main road, the responsible offices are to follow the old precedents and escort him with the imperial equipage."
units.literal: When the army approaches by the main road, the responsible offices are to follow the old precedents in detail and escort him with the imperial equipage."
